ChatMessage.content: How many days of annual leave does a Manager get?
A Manager is entitled to 18 working days of annual leave per calendar year (Section 2.6).
What is the medical subsidy cap per year?
The medical subsidy is subject to a maximum of S$500 per calendar year per employee (Section 3.1).
What is the notice period for an Executive who resigns?
The notice period for an employee in the "Executive and below" grade who intends to resign is one (1) month (Section 9.1).
Who sits on the interview panel for a Coach-level hire?

For a Coach-level hire, the interview panel comprises the following members:
1. Chief Executive Officer
2. Board Member
3. Representative from the High Performance Standing Committee
4. SSI Representative
(Section 1.2)
Can employees carry forward annual leave? What is the limit?
Yes, a maximum of seven (7) days of unconsumed annual leave earned in a calendar year may be carried forward to the following year (Section 2.6 b).
Does MAF provide an internet/WFH stipend?
I don't have this information in the HR policy.
If a Manager takes childcare leave and later resigns, can the unused childcare leave offset their notice period?
No, childcare leave cannot be used to offset the notice period on resignation (Section 2.10).

1.4 Probation
All  new  employees  serve  a  probationary  period  of  three  (3)  months,  which  may  be  extended  by  up  to  a
further three (3) months at the discretion of the Foundation. During probation, either party may terminate
the employment by giving one (1) week’s notice in writing or payment of one week’s salary in lieu of notice.
Confirmation  of  employment  is  subject  to  a  satisfactory  probation  review  conducted  by  the  employee’s
immediate supervisor.
2. Terms & Conditions of Service
2.1 Appointment Letter
The Letter of Appointment will include the following particulars:
n
Full name of the Employer and the Employee
n
Job title, main duties, and responsibilities
n
Start date of employment
n
Duration of employment (if the employee is on a fixed-term contract)
n
Daily working hours, number of working days per week, and rest day
n
Salary period, basic salary, fixed allowances, and fixed deductions
n
Overtime compensation arrangements (including Off-in-Lieu)
n
Bonuses and incentives
n
Type and quantum of leave
n
Medical and dental benefits (including insurance coverage)
n
Probation period
n
Notice period
n
Place of work

2.15 Off-in-Lieu (OIL)
Employees who work on weekends and public holidays may be compensated with Off-in-Lieu (OIL), which
must  be  consumed  within  the  same  calendar  year  and  cannot  be  carried  forward.  Approval  must  be
obtained from the Chief Executive Officer, with the HR and Finance Executive copied, by email indicating
the name of the event, the date, and the hours worked. Guidelines:
a)
There is no encashment of OIL. OIL is valid only for work performed during MAF-organised or
MAF-supported events and competitions.
b)
OIL is granted based on the number of hours worked on weekends and public holidays: for four (4)
hours or less, time off in lieu of four (4) hours on a working day is granted; for more than four (4)
hours, a full day off on a working day is granted.

4. Remuneration, Annual Wage Supplement & Bonuses
The Annual Wage Supplement (AWS, or “13th-month” payment) and any performance bonus are granted
based  on  good  work  performance  and  are  paid  at  the  discretion  of  the  Board.  They  are  guided  by  the

the financial health of the Foundation. To be eligible for the full AWS, an employee must have served the
full  calendar  year;  otherwise,  the  AWS  is  pro-rated.  Salaries  are  paid  monthly,  on  or  before  the  last
working  day  of  each  month,  by  direct  credit  to  the  employee’s  designated  bank  account,  with  the
appropriate CPF contributions made in accordance with the law.

7. Workplace Harassment & Grievance Handling
7.1 Zero-Tolerance Policy
The  Foundation  is  committed  to  providing  a  safe  and  respectful  workplace.  Harassment,  bullying,
discrimination,  and  victimisation  of  any  kind—whether  physical,  verbal,  written,  or  online—will  not  be
tolerated and may constitute grounds for disciplinary action up to and including dismissal.
7.2 Reporting a Grievance
An employee who experiences or witnesses harassment, or who has a workplace grievance, should raise
it through the following channels:
1.
Raise the matter informally with the immediate supervisor, where appropriate.
2.
If unresolved, or if the supervisor is the subject of the complaint, submit a written complaint to the
Manager, Human Resources & Administration.
3.
Serious matters are escalated to the Chief Executive Officer, who will commence an investigation.
Where the complaint concerns the Chief Executive Officer, it is referred directly to the Chairman of
the Board.
All complaints are treated in strict confidence so far as is reasonably practicable. The Foundation prohibits
any retaliation against an employee who makes a complaint in good faith.
8. Information Technology & Data Protection
8.1 Acceptable Use

The Foundation’s IT systems, devices, email, and internet access are provided primarily for business use.
Employees  must  not  use  these  resources  to  access,  store,  or  distribute  unlawful,  offensive,  or  infringing
material,   and   must   take   reasonable   care   to   protect   their   login   credentials   and   devices   against
unauthorised access.
8.2 Personal Data Protection
The  Foundation  collects,  uses,  and  discloses  personal  data  in  accordance  with  the  Personal  Data
Protection Act 2012 (PDPA). Employees who handle the personal data of members, athletes, donors, or
fellow  staff  must  do  so  only  for  legitimate  business  purposes,  must  keep  such  data  secure,  and  must

3. Employee Benefits
3.1 Medical & Dental Benefits
Employees are eligible for medical and dental benefits after completing at least three (3) months of service
with the Foundation.
n
The medical subsidy is subject to a maximum of S$500 per calendar year per employee.
n
The dental subsidy is subject to a maximum of S$250 per calendar year per employee.
n
Any unused balance cannot be carried forward to the following year.
n
The Foundation maintains a Group Hospitalisation & Surgical (GHS) and Group Personal Accident
insurance scheme covering all confirmed employees.
3.1.1 Sick Leave & Hospitalisation Leave
A  confirmed  employee  is  granted  paid  sick  leave  of  up  to  fourteen  (14)  days  per  calendar  year  for
outpatient (non-hospitalisation) cases, or up to sixty (60) days per calendar year where hospitalisation is
necessary  (the  60  days  being  inclusive  of  the  14  outpatient  days).  The  employee  must  inform  their
immediate  supervisor  within  two  (2)  hours  of  the  start  of  the  working  day,  and  submit  a  valid  medical
certificate  to  HR  as  soon  as  possible;  otherwise  the  absence  will  be  treated  as  unpaid  leave  with  a
corresponding salary deduction.

A working father is entitled to four (4) weeks of Government-Paid Paternity Leave (GPPL), in line with the
enhanced statutory entitlement, provided that:
a)
the child is a Singapore citizen;
b)
he is, or has been, lawfully married to the child’s mother between conception and birth; and

he has served the Foundation for a continuous period of at least three (3) months before the birth of
the child.
